newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CANDIDATES FOR FIFA'S 1996 WORLD PLAYER AWARD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CANDIDATES FOR FIFA'S 1996 WORLD PLAYER AWARD.

text.p: Following are profiles of Ronaldo, Alan Shearer and George Weah, the three candidates for FIFA's 1996 World Player of the Year award. The winner will be announced in Lisbon on Monday.
Career path: Social Ramos Club, Sao Cristovao, Cruzeiro (all Brazil), PSV Eindhoven (Netherlands) 1994-1996. Joined Barcelona in July 1996.

The shaven-headed Brazilian has been dubbed "the extraterrestrial" since his arrival in Spain, which has never seen anything quite like him. Has claimed a number of stunning strikes for Barca, picking the ball up in midfield and heading straight for goal at speed. Gifted with extraordinary strength and balance, appears to bounce off defenders as he heads goalwards. Has also earned praise for his refusal to dive in the box in search of penalties. Has gone off the boil slightly since suffering an injury in November but played brilliantly against Deportivo Coruna a fortnight ago and scored at Camp Nou on Monday to end a 56-day goal drought. Career path: Southampton 1988-92, Blackburn 1992-96 (both England). Joined Newcastle in July 1996.

Unquestionably the most complete striker in British football at present. At his best in the box, where he turns and strikes with unerring accuracy, but is also happy drifting out to the flanks to pick up the ball or falling back into midfield to win it. Made his name at Blackburn where he scored 112 goals in 138 league appearances and became the first man to score 100 goals in the premier league. Then proved he could do the same for England at the European championship where he was top scorer with five goals. Ice-cool temperament makes him the ideal dead-ball specialist and led to him being named England captain this year. The world's costliest player shows no sign of faltering now he is

Career path: Young Survivors, Bongrange, Invincible Eleven, Mighty Barolle (all Liberia), Tonnerre Yaounde (Cameroon), Monaco 1988-92, Paris St Germain 1992-95 (both France). joined AC Milan in May 1995.

Current FIFA world player of the year, lauded as the "Godfather of Liberian soccer" in his home country, whose national side he has kept afloat by bankrolling expenses and organising kit sponsorship. Has played around 50 times for his country, usually in midfield rather than attack as that is where the side are at their weakest. A tremendous athlete, he established himself in France with his aggressive runs on goal and power in the air. Scored one of the goals of the year on the opening day of the current Italian season, picking up the ball deep in his own penalty area and beating half the Verona team before finding the net.
